comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose significant year-over-year revenue growth in their respective high-growth technology segments for fiscal year 2024, driven by artificial intelligence and data center demand. NVDA's automotive segment grew by 21% to $1.1 billion, primarily due to self-driving platforms. Similarly, AMD's Data Center segment, a key growth engine, surged by 94% to $12.6 billion, driven by AMD Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. While both companies benefited from AI-related hardware sales, NVDA's disclosure focuses on the automotive application of these technologies, whereas AMD's disclosure highlights the broader data center infrastructure expansion.

sentences.text: Automotive revenue for the fiscal year 2024 was up 21%.
The increase primarily reflected growth in self-driving platforms.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.
